name: Aldar Headquarters
features: A 23-floor office building shaped as a single circular disc, held by a diagonal steel grid.
view: front elevation of the disc face, showing the circle set into the ground and its diagrid
note: Only Commons file is File:Al Dar Hq architecutal view.jpg (641x350, CC BY-SA 4.0), below 800px. Wikipedia: 110 m, 23 floors, steel diagrid, circle sunk into the ground by a golden-ratio depth. Diagrid density is simplified.

name: Sheikh Zayed Bridge
features: Sweeping steel arches that rise and fall along the road deck as it crosses the channel to Abu Dhabi island.
note: The Arabic-named file (3264x2448, Flickr) is titled after the bridge. Abu Dhabi 2013 - panoramio (1280x685) is in the bridge category but untitled; check it shows the arches.

name: UAE Pavilion, Expo 2020
features: Roof of 28 carbon-fibre wings that open and close, shaped like a falcon in flight.
commons_category: Category:United Arab Emirates Pavilion at EXPO 2020
note: 32 Flickr photos (6720x4480, CC BY 2.0, Brazilian government) in the category; first one checked by metadata only. Expo opened in 2021; building completed 2020.

name: Dubai Frame
features: Two 150 m towers joined by a glass-floored bridge, framing old Dubai on one side and the new city on the other.
note: Built by Hyder Consulting from Donis's competition design; 150 m tall, 95.5 m wide. UAE has no freedom of panorama, so these files may be deleted later.

name: Dubai World Trade Centre
features: Dubai's first skyscraper, a 184 m tower opened in 1979 as Sheikh Rashid Tower; a landmark of Gulf modernism.

photos.file: File:Dubai World Trade Centre and skyline.jpg
File:Etisalat Tower 2, Dubai World Trade Centre, and Dubai World Trade Centre Residence on 14 September 2007.jpg

note: Wikipedia gives 184 m, opened 26 February 1979 as Sheikh Rashid Tower, by John R. Harris and Partners.

name: Al Bahr Towers
features: About 2,000 umbrella-like screens, a moving mashrabiya, open and close automatically with the sunlight.

photos.file: File:Fountain and Al Bahr Towers - panoramio.jpg

note: Only one free file (5184x3456, Panoramio) and no Commons category; a fountain is in the foreground, so check the towers are clear. If not, this is a good drawing candidate.

name: The Opus
features: A glass cube with a free-form void carved through its middle, splitting it into two towers joined above and below.
view: front elevation of the cube, with the free-form void cut through it and its inner glass face beyond; lines mark every second floor
note: No Commons category and no files found. Sources: two towers read as one cube; eight-storey free-form void; four-storey atrium links the towers at ground level and an asymmetric 38 m wide, three-storey bridge at 71 m. Height given as about 93 m by one source. The void outline is simplified from published descriptions; houses the ME Dubai hotel and offices.

name: Dubai Opera
features: Plan shaped like a dhow: the stage and seats in the bow, foyers and drop-off in the long hull.
note: No free exterior photo: Category:Dubai Opera House holds only interior and event photos (e.g. File:Inside the Dubai Opera.jpg, 2736x3648, CC BY 2.0). Not drawn: sources give 44 m height and say the dhow shape is in plan, with faceted inclined glazing, but no length or elevation, so the silhouette can't be drawn with confidence.

name: House of Wisdom
features: A thin floating roof overhangs the two-storey glass library by 15 m on every side, shading it from the desert sun.
view: long elevation: the flat roof plane overhanging a two-storey glazed box wrapped in vertical aluminium screens
note: No Commons category or files found. Sources: two-storey rectilinear glass building, roof overhangs 15 m in all directions, carried by four internal cores (no perimeter columns), fixed aluminium screens outside. Proportions estimated from the 13,000 m2 two-level floor area; the screen spacing is schematic. Opened 2020 for Sharjah World Book Capital 2019.

name: Aspire Tower (The Torch Doha)
features: A 300 m concrete core with floors cantilevered off it, wrapped in steel mesh and topped by a lattice torch.
view: front elevation: flared base, slim waist and wider top (about 70, 27 and 45 m across), the lattice cone above the 238 m observatory and the petal-shaped flame holder
note: The Commons category holds only Category:Incidental views of Aspire Tower (park panoramas, fireworks, a sunset silhouette); no file shows the tower clearly. Built for the 2006 Asian Games (held the flame); Wikipedia dates conflict (2007 completion). Outline follows the published widths; mesh and lattice lines are schematic. The pool cantilevered at 80 m is left out.

name: Emirates Towers
features: Twin towers of 355 m and 309 m, an office tower and a hotel, rising from one podium on Sheikh Zayed Road.
note: Only one free file is filed under the towers themselves (Sh5-zayed-road.jpg, 2592x1944, in both Category:Emirates Office Tower and Category:Jumeirah Emirates Towers Hotel), a street view; check the towers are clear. Opened 15 April 2000.

name: One Za'abeel
features: Two towers on either side of a highway, threaded by The Link: 230 m long, 100 m up, cantilevering 67 m.
note: Only file in the category is a 4000x3000 CC0 road view, also filed under Dubai World Trade Centre; check the towers and The Link are clear. If not, this is worth drawing, but the tower widths and gap aren't published, so a drawing would need a plan or elevation source first.

name: Al Thumama Stadium
by: Ibrahim M. Jaidah, Arab Engineering Bureau
features: A round stadium shaped like the taqiyah, the woven cap worn by men and boys across the Middle East.
note: One exterior file (4000x1800). Heerim also listed as architect in Wikipedia's infobox.

name: Stadium 974
features: Built from 974 recycled shipping containers and a modular steel frame, designed to be taken apart and moved.
note: One exterior file (4000x2252, CC0). Still on its original site as of December 2025.

name: Lusail Stadium
features: Host stadium of the 2022 World Cup final, designed by Foster + Partners with Populous.

photos.file: File:Aerial view of Lusail Stadium during the daytime.png

note: Aerial view (3838x2160, CC BY 3.0). Wikipedia gives built 2017-2021, inaugurated 2022; Wikipedia does not describe the facade or roof.

name: Al Bayt Stadium
features: Shaped like the bayt al sha'ar, the black-and-white tent of Gulf nomads, stretched over the whole stadium.
note: One exterior file (1536x1191). Wikipedia names Dar Al-Handasah in the text but gmp in the infobox; check the credit. Inaugurated 30 November 2021.

name: Qatar University
features: Precast octagonal modules on a grid, each classroom topped by a wind tower for cool air and soft daylight.
note: File:Qatar University.Campus.jpg (1637x1310) is the only large general campus view; check it shows the wind-tower buildings. First phase opened February 1985; Arup were engineers; shortlisted for the Aga Khan Award (1989 cycle).

name: King Fahd International Stadium
features: A ring of roof canopies held by 24 columns on a 247 m circle shades the stands from the desert sun.

photos.file: File:King Fahd International Stadium, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, April 2014.jpg

note: 14 files; the first (2048x1536) is an exterior, the second an interior. Wikipedia: roof held by 24 columns on a 247 m circle, opened 1987; with Michael K.C. Cheah and Partners.

name: King Khalid International Airport
features: Triangular terminals, and a Royal Terminal whose roof of 33 arched sections rises 30 m.
note: Large category; the panoramio file (4352x3264) is titled Terminal 1, the second is an aerial view (1280x888).

name: Maraya
features: A concert hall wrapped in 9,740 m2 of mirror, a box that reflects the desert canyon until it nearly disappears.
note: Ten 4000x2252 CC BY 4.0 photos from January 2026. In use from December 2018; Guinness record as largest mirrored building on 26 December 2019.

name: Sheikh Jaber Al-Ahmad Cultural Centre
features: Four buildings around courtyards off a civic plaza, wrapped in steel envelopes clad in titanium panels.
commons_category: Category:Sheikh Jaber Al Ahmad Cultural Centre

photos.file: File:Sheikh Jaber Al Ahmad Cultural Centre Kuwait.jpg

note: One exterior file (3024x4032, CC0). Also called the Kuwait Opera House.

name: Grand Mosque of Kuwait
features: A 26 m dome and 74 m minaret over courtyards, Makiya's modern reading of Islamic precedent.

photos.file: File:Kuwait City Grand Mosque Exterior North Facade 1.jpg

note: 95 files including many exterior views (4569x3217, CC BY 4.0). Construction 1979-1986.

name: Queen Alia International Airport
features: A roof of 127 shallow concrete domes on columns, inspired by Bedouin tents, shades the terminal.

photos.file: File:Queen Alia International Airport - New Terminal - 2013.JPG
File:Jordan 2021 P369 Amman Queen Alia International Airport.jpg

note: Large category with several exterior views. New terminal inaugurated March 2013. The airport is at Zizya, south of Amman.

name: Feynan Ecolodge
features: A desert lodge shaped like a caravanserai around a courtyard, lit by hand-made candles at night.

photos.file: File:Feynan Eco Lodge with slats to keep the walls in shade.JPG
File:32 Dana Feynan Trail - The Feynan Lodge - panoramio.jpg

note: Five files, three large exteriors. In the Dana Biosphere Reserve.

name: Holiday Inn Beirut
features: A 26-storey hotel open only a year before the civil war; its gutted frame still stands as a war memory.

photos.file: File:Former Holiday Inn in downtown Beirut.jpg

note: Three large exterior photos. Built 1971-74; fought over in the 1975-76 Battle of the Hotels and left a stripped concrete frame.

name: The Egg (Beirut City Center)
features: An unfinished concrete cinema dome, started in 1965 and stopped by the civil war, now a city landmark.

photos.file: File:The Egg cinema in Beirut Lebanon.jpg

note: Never completed: 1965 is the start of construction. No dedicated Commons category was found by search; the files are there.

name: Monument to the Unknown Soldier (1959)
features: Chadirji turned the brick arch of Ctesiphon into a thin concrete arch in Firdos Square.
commons_category: Category:Monument to the Unknown Soldier, Baghdad

photos.file: File:Monument to the Unknown Soldier, Baghdad.jpg

extras.file: File:Unknown Soldier Monument under construction, Baghdad, 1959.jpg

note: Demolished around 1982-83 and replaced by a statue. The usable photo is a 1960s postcard (1600x1120, PD). The Commons category also holds a photo of the different 1982 monument (glass spire file); don't mix them up. Extras' sizes beyond the first weren't checked.

name: Federation of Industries Building
features: One of Chadirji's brick office buildings, his search for a modern architecture rooted in Iraq.

extras.file: File:Postcard showing new architecture of Baghdad, 1966.jpg

note: Three recent photos (about 2000px, from Al-Khilani Square). The 1966 date comes from the postcard's Commons description. Features line kept general: check the brick detail in the photos before adding specifics.

name: Zayed National Museum
features: Five steel towers shaped like falcon feathers, 83-123 m high, act as chimneys drawing air through the galleries.

photos.file: File:Zayed national Museum front entrance - 23 may 2026.jpg

note: Only one exterior (3024x4032, front entrance, May 2026); check the towers show. Opened 3 December 2025; a 30 m external hill links the bases of the wings.

name: Dhahran Air Terminal
features: Yamasaki's civil air terminal for Dhahran, which won the AIA First Honor Award in 1963.

photos.file: File:591 Cameron terminal at Dhahran finished - USACE-p15141coll5-15769.jpeg
File:473 Cameron terminal at Dhahran driveway - USACE-p15141coll5-15655.jpeg

extras.file: File:Dhahran Civil Air Terminal, Saudi Arabia, under construction - USACE-p15141coll5-509.jpeg

note: US Army Corps of Engineers photos (PD) plus 1960s photos. The Commons description says the AIA gave Yamasaki its First Honor Award for the terminal in 1963. The terminal also appears on Saudi banknotes in the category. Concepts are generic; check against the photos.

name: Cairo Opera House
features: A gift from Japan to Egypt, built 1985-88 to give Cairo a new opera house after the Khedivial Opera.
note: Many photos in the category. Built 1985-1988 by Japanese and Egyptian architects; Nikken Sekkei is the usual credit.

name: National Museum of Egyptian Civilization
features: Egypt's museum of civilisation in Old Cairo, home of the royal mummies since the 2021 Golden Parade.
note: Hundreds of files; first one titled with the museum (4032x3024), not checked whether it's an exterior. Partly opened 2017, officially inaugurated April 2021.

name: Azadi Stadium
features: Iran's national stadium, opened in 1971 for about 120,000 people and main venue of the 1974 Asian Games.
note: Many files and year subcategories. Opened 17 October 1971; parts of the sports complex planned with SOM.

name: Terra, the Sustainability Pavilion
features: A 130 m solar canopy on a single central column over galleries sunk into the ground, with 18 rotating Energy Trees.
note: No Commons category or files found. Not drawn: sources give the canopy width (130-135 m, angled and oval, 70 m cantilever) but no height or section, so the profile can't be drawn to proportion. A Grimshaw section would settle it.

name: Masdar Institute
features: Labs and housing on shaded narrow streets: undulating screened facades, ETFE-cushion walls and a modern wind tower.
note: Commons category holds only people/event subcategories, no building photos. Not drawn: it is a group of buildings, and the sources describe the facade systems but not the massing or storey counts well enough for an accurate elevation.

name: Aïshti Foundation
features: Galleries and shops behind a red aluminium-tube screen whose zigzag pattern recalls the mashrabiya.
note: No Commons category or files found. Not drawn: sources describe the facade and a block 'rotated on one edge', but give no height or storey count. At Jal el Dib on the coast north of Beirut.

name: Kuwait National Museum
features: Concrete museum buildings set around a central garden, like a courtyard house, by the planner of Casablanca.
note: Only building file is File:Kwnmuseum.jpg (543x308), below 800px. Not drawn: sources disagree on four or five buildings, and the 28 m open metal sun-roof described by Archnet may not have been built. Competition 1960, built 1977-81, opened 1983; damaged in 1990.

name: Stone Garden
features: A 13-storey tower of hand-combed earth and cement, cut by openings of many sizes that hold gardens.
note: No Commons files found. Not drawn: the sources confirm 13 storeys, about 50 m and irregular openings, but not the silhouette (whether the top steps or slopes) or where the openings fall. Survived the 2020 port explosion.
